title: Telemetry Onboarding Sprint Workbook + Trace Playlists
content:
Purpose:
This is a hands-on sprint workbook for new telemetry stewards and engineers joining the observability team. The goal is to run a small, timeboxed onboarding sprint (3–5 days) that leaves a candidate able to: 1) author a basic metric contract for an inference path; 2) add minimal tracing spans to a service handler; 3) wire a compact dashboard panel with SLI/SLO and an investigation query.

Why this exists (context):
- We have great long-form playbooks, but new joiners still struggle to translate theory into practiced artifacts (metric contract + trace annotations + dashboard panel) inside the token-serving stack.
- This workbook prioritizes small, repeatable exercises and trace "playlists" (curated capture + query patterns) so a steward can own an end-to-end visibility slice quickly.

Audience:
- New observability stewards, platform engineers onboarding to inference, solutions engineers learning to instrument customers' private deployments.

Sprint outline (3-day condensed):
Day 0 (prep): clone telemetry config repo, get dev env with local trace sampler on, open the referenced PR and Confluence page.
Day 1: Metric contract + lightweight dashboard panel
  - Exercise A: Select an endpoint (e.g., /v1/generate) with a short user story: "single-turn chat generation, 95th percentile latency < 250ms for tier-dedicated customers".
  - Author a metric contract (name, type, tags, aggregation, owner, retention tier). Short template to fill:
    * metric_name: inference.service.v1.latency_ms
    * unit: milliseconds
    * aggregation: p50,p95,p99,avg
    * cardinality_tags: model_name, deployment_tier, tenant_id (hashed)
    * owner: eng-serving-runtime@redwood.team
    * alert_threshold: p95 > 250ms for 10m
  - Add the metric to metrics.yaml in telemetry-config and run linter.
  - Dashboard task: make a single panel showing p95 latency and a micro-SLI line (green/yellow/red) with TTL annotation for cache-warmth. Save the dashboard under /dashboards/inference/quickpanels.
Day 2: Tracing additions + trace playlist exercises
  - Exercise B: Add two spans to request flow: "handler.receive_input" and "runtime.kv_cache.lookup" with clear span attributes. Minimal spec:
    * handler.receive_input - attribs: request_id, input_len, model_hint
    * runtime.kv_cache.lookup - attribs: cache_hit (bool), kv_latency_ms, key_hash
  - Instrumentation acceptance: spans show in the UI within 30s, attributes are searchable, span duration correlates to latency metric.
  - Trace playlist: run the curated set of traffic patterns and capture traces: cold-starts (10x cold calls), prefix-heavy requests (long context), kv-eviction spike (burst with randomized keys).
  - Postmortem mini-exercise: pick one captured trace, write a 1-paragraph hypothesis (root cause) and next action.

Trace Playlists (curated sequences to run in staging):
- Playlist: Cold-Start Detective
  1) Clear runtime cache (script: tools/clear_cache.sh)
  2) Send 50 sequential distinct requests spaced 200ms apart at baseline payload (50 tokens)
  3) Capture traces, filter for handler.receive_input and runtime.kv_cache.lookup spans, export top 10 slowest
  Expected signals: high p95 latency, long kv_cache.lookup durations on first N requests, progressive warm-up in metrics.

- Playlist: Token-Expansion Hotpath
  1) Use long-prefix template (context ~2048 tokens) with request size 512 tokens
  2) Run 30 concurrent requests for 2 minutes
  3) Inspect traces for tokenization slow-paths and GPU memcpy spikes (span names: tokenizer.split, runtime.attention_kernel)
  Expected signals: broader latency distribution, potential kernel fallback traces.

- Playlist: Eviction Storm
  1) Emit synthetic keys across 20 tenants at high cardinality to force kv churn
  2) Run burst load: 500 qps for 30s
  3) Search spans for kv_cache.eviction and runtime.kv_cache.lookup with cache_hit=false
  Expected signals: increased CPU on sidecars, higher p99 latency on inference, metric drift in cache_hit ratio.

Metric + Trace mapping cheat-sheet (compact):
- inference.service.v1.latency_ms -> traces: handler.receive_input (entry), model.decode (token loop)
- inference.service.v1.token_count -> traces: tokenizer.split, model.decode (attributes: tokens_emitted)
- inference.cache.hit_rate -> traces: runtime.kv_cache.lookup (cache_hit attr)

Dashboard checklist (minimum for a panel to be accepted):
- Title: includes intent ("p95 latency - single-turn")
- Query: uses aggregated p95 over 5m with moving-window annotation for cache warmups
- SLI visualization: a discrete SLI line with thresholds and time-in-breach shading
- Linked trace samples: panel has a 1-click link to saved trace search with the same filters (model_name + deployment_tier)
- Cost note: panel queries limited to sample rate <= 1% for long-range views, full-coverage in last 1h only
- Ownership: owner field set and runbook link added to panel metadata

Acceptance criteria (what "done" looks like):
- Metric contract merged to telemetry-config and linter passes (CI link in PR).
- Two spans appear in trace UI and attributes are searchable within 1 hour in staging.
- Dashboard panel created and preview shared with two reviewers (eng-observability, eng-serving-runtime).
- One trace from the playlist with root cause hypothesis and an owner assigned for next action.

Common pitfalls & debugging hints:
- If spans don't appear: verify tracer env vars (OTEL_EXPORTER, SERVICE_NAME), ensure sampling probability in local sampler is >0.05 for playlist runs.
- Missing attributes: check instrumentation uses string keys and avoid nested objects; attributes show only primitive types in our backend.
- Dashboards showing stale metrics: confirm metric tag cardinality (tenant_id should be hashed) and that retention tier is not archive.

Follow-ups & growth tasks:
- Convert the workbook into a short recorded lab (15–20 min) for self-service onboarding.
- Automate the trace playlists to run as CI probes after rollout PRs for model/quantization changes.
- Expand metric contract template to include cost-sensitivity annotation (expected token cost per 1k requests).

Unresolved questions (for sprint retro):
- Should we standardize a single span naming prefix (we currently have handler.* and runtime.* but some teams use service.*)?
- What default sampling rate do we require for production canaries to ensure reproducible trace-driven rollbacks?

Notes-to-self / quick links:
- Confluence onboarding checklist: https://confluence.internal/redwood/obs-onboarding
- Local trace UI: http://localhost:16686 (OTEL collector dev config)
- Useful scripts: tools/run_playlist.sh, tools/collect_traces.sh

Small checklist to hand to a reviewer before approving a steward's work:
- Metric contract sanity: tag list limited to 3 high-cardinality keys
- Spans show correct durations and have minimal attribute set
- Dashboard has owner, runbook link, and 1 sample trace linked

If you run this with a new hire, please ping #obs-oncall and drop the PR link into the sprint thread so reviewers can quick-approve in <24h.

---
End of workbook. This is intentionally compact — the idea is to force doing rather than reading. Add notes in the Confluence page after each run with tracer links and a short one-paragraph finding.
